findings.title: .dde substring filter has false positives on legitimate file/folder names (carryover from round 1)
findings.description: Both `scanMarkdownFiles` (L602) and `hasMarkdownFiles` (L642) still reject any URL whose `.path` *contains* the substring `.dde`. This matches not only the intended `.dde/` workspace folder but also legitimate names: `my.ddefile.md`, `.ddesomething.md`, folders like `.dde-cache/`, `widget.dde/`. Round 1 minor finding was scoped out of the round-1 fix — flagging again so it stays on the radar.
findings.impact: Availability/correctness only — no security impact. A user with a folder named `widget.dde/` containing legitimate notes would silently see them omitted from Insight summaries.
findings.recommendation: Tighten to a path-component match: `guard !url.pathComponents.contains(".dde") else { continue }`. Defer to a follow-up refactor that unifies the four `.dde` filter sites in this file.

findings.title: Symlink-escape rejection still logs full filesystem path via NSLog (carryover from round 1)
findings.description: When containment fails, the helper logs `"[Insight] Skipped symlink escape: \(url.path)"` (L609). `NSLog` writes to system unified log. The path may include the workspace root, user folder, and the actual filename of the off-scope file — precisely the path the security control just decided the user should NOT have visibility into. Carryover from round 1.
findings.impact: Information disclosure to local log readers and sysdiagnose recipients. Low likelihood of exploitation in single-user macOS, but path data ends up in persistent logs the user is likely unaware of.
findings.recommendation: Log basename only or gate full-path logging behind a debug flag: `NSLog("[Insight] Skipped symlink escape: %@", url.lastPathComponent)`. Apply the same review to scope_hint rejection logging in Task 4.
findings.cwe: CWE-532 (Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File)

findings.title: Resource cap order-of-operations still appends before checking (carryover from round 1)
findings.description: At L613-616 the helper still appends to `results` BEFORE the cap check, then `count > limit` triggers and `results.count` is `limit + 1`. The error message `"found \(count)+ markdown files"` therefore always says `found 501+` (the `+` implies more), but enumeration halts at exactly 501. Tech-spec acceptance criterion (`> 500 fails, == 500 passes`) is satisfied — boundary correct — but the reported count is misleading. Carryover from round 1.
findings.impact: None security-wise — DoS protection works as intended (immediate halt at 501). Cosmetic/UX nit only.
findings.recommendation: Either swap the order to check before append (`if results.count >= limit { return .failure(.folderTooLarge(count: limit + 1, limit: limit)) }; results.append(url)`), or change the message to `"more than \(limit) markdown files"` to drop the misleading `+`.

round1FollowUp.criticalFinding: Symlink containment check bypassable via sibling-folder prefix collision

verification.bothCallSitesFixed: yes — scanMarkdownFiles (L581-608) and hasMarkdownFiles (L627-644) both build resolvedFolderPrefix and use `resolvedFile == resolvedFolderPath || resolvedFile.hasPrefix(resolvedFolderPrefix)`
verification.trailingSlashHandling: correct — `hasSuffix("/") ? path : path + "/"` avoids `//` artifact; URL.standardizedFileURL.path strips trailing slashes so the guard is defensive but correctly handles the rare root-`/` edge case
verification.equalityFallbackSafety: safe — `resolvedFile == resolvedFolderPath` is defensive (folder URL itself never surfaces in enumerator output for a directory). Cannot match any sibling because exact string equality on the resolved folder path is unique. No new bypass.
verification.symlinkResolveOrder: correct — `resolvingSymlinksInPath().standardizedFileURL.path` (resolve BEFORE standardize) at L581, L604, L627, L643. Matches tech-spec Decision 10 §6 mandate.
verification.noSimilarPatternsInNewCode: confirmed — only the two fixed call sites in the new Recursive Insight code (L540-648) use path-prefix containment. Other `hasPrefix` usages in WorkspaceManager.swift (L76, L118, L125, L673, L761) are pre-existing and outside Task 2 scope.
verification.exploitWalkthrough: For folder `/x/foo`: resolvedFolderPath=`/x/foo`, resolvedFolderPrefix=`/x/foo/`. Sibling escape `/x/foobar/secret.md` is NOT equal to `/x/foo` AND does NOT start with `/x/foo/` → correctly rejected. Round 1 reproducer is now blocked.

regressionChecks.resourceCap: unchanged — still appends then checks `count > limit` returning `.failure` (cap behavior identical to round 1)
regressionChecks.hiddenFilesAndPackageDescendants: unchanged — `[.skipsHiddenFiles, .skipsPackageDescendants]` still passed to both enumerators (L593, L636)
regressionChecks.includingPropertiesForKeysChange: noted but benign — reduced from `[.isSymbolicLinkKey]` to `nil`. The new check does not depend on the symlink-flag prefetch; it resolves every URL via `resolvingSymlinksInPath()` regardless. Minor performance win, no security weakening.
